notes.title: Week 1 - Next Content Update and Post-Launch Update
notes.notes:

We’re focused on stability fixes and also working on new content.[/p][p][/p][h1]Next Content Update![/h1][p]The team is working in two parallel tracks. Part of the team is working on stability and the other part on our next update that brings new content. We’re currently working on:[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/dd8c1ff17d842c6a64577db45dcf54e41a4788f6.jpg"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Hangar vendors[/b]: Got too many credits on your hands? notes.title: Early Access Price and Roadmap
notes.notes: [p]Ten days till launch! 🚀[/p][p][/p][p][b]Jump Space will be available on 19th of September.[/b][/p][p][b]Release times: 7AM PT | 10AM ET | 3PM BST | 4PM CEST[/b][/p][p][b]Game price: $19.99 | £16.75 | €19.50[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]Jump Space will not be in the Steam Autumn Sale.[/b] [/p][p][/p][p]As development progresses, the price may increase (for example when leaving Early Access). If that happens, we'll let you know in advance. We haven’t set a date for version 1.0 or decided exactly when the price will change.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b][u]Early Access Development Roadmap[/u][/b][/h3][p][b]This is a work in progress and subject to change. This image is in our Steam page description too.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/9b6ef9d1752d9e152cb331205beb73e63d833d3c.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What's new since the June Demo?[/b][/h3][p]So for those who tried the June Demo, Jump Space has grown a lot. We've expanded the story, added new missions and goals, and even brought more characters into the Hangar for you to interact with. Here is a brief overview of what you'll play on September 19th:[/p][p] [/p][p]Mission Types: [b]9[/b][/p][p]Playable sectors: [b]50+[/b][/p][p]Unlockable Galaxy Regions: [b]4[/b][/p][p]Ships to Pilot: [b]2[/b][/p][p]Ship components: [b]26[/b][/p][p]Player Weapons: [b]8[/b][/p][p]Ship Enemies: [b]16[/b][/p][p]Ground Enemies: [b]11[/b][/p][p][/p][p]We'll be expanding on all of the above during the Early Access.[/p][list][*][p][b]Mission Types[/b] is what the final sector objective is, as a sort of "Finale" to the mission.[/p][p]If you played our demo in June, that had [b]2 [/b]mission types: Salvage and Cargo Ship.[/p][p]So there are 9 mission types for you to play.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p][b]Sectors[/b] is what we're calling the playable areas within a mission. They're levels basically. We have 50+ of them so far, compared to the handful that were in the demo.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p][b]Galaxy Regions [/b]is each section of the big galaxy map. New content will unlock as you explore new regions of the galaxy, and we hope to add different themes and biomes to make each region more distinct.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]You will start with the Catamaran [b]ship[/b], and work to restore that to full operations.[/p][p]As you complete missions, you may stumble upon a wreck of a 2nd ship.[/p][p]With a little work you'll get to pilot that one as well.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]We have added plenty more [b]ship components [/b]compared to the demo, and this is where you can really start building your ship in different ways and upgrade your favorite components.[/p][p]More components will be added and reworked as we update mechanics like the Ship Shields and Scanner.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]We've added one more [b]weapon[/b], the LMG, since the demo. Total player weapons are now 8.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Some new [b]enemies [/b]have also appeared, and we look forward to introducing more enemy variety in the future.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]The [b]Current Content[/b] section of the roadmap image will be updated to give a brief, accurate overview of our progress as we release new updates that increases the numbers listed here.[/p][p][/p][p]Not every single new piece of content, bug fix or improvement to a mechanic or level will be featured on the roadmap. That would result in 100+ small boxes. :ggxxacmay:[/p][p]Just so that you're aware that there's more coming inbetween these bigger things worth visualizing.[/p][p][/p][h3][b][u]Chapters[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Our development journey will be divided up into "Chapters" that stretch over a longer period of time.[/p][p][b]Chapters will consist of several updates[/b] until we've added everything listed in that chapter.[/p][p]Only then do we move on to the next chapter.[/p][p]We've already marked "Text Chat" and "Lobby Browser" in green as "completed" since they have been added to the game and will be available at launch.[/p][p][/p][p]Game development is tricky, and it's hard to accurately estimate when things are completed.[/p][p]Doing Chapters instead of listing many mapped out updates gives us more flexibility, and we avoid disappointing players if a planned update gets delayed a few weeks for example.[/p][p][/p][p]Especially since the roadmap will constantly change based on feedback. [b]Chapter 1 and 2 might look bigger[/b] a few months from now, depending on what you all think we should prioritize after playing the Early Access and what resources we have to cram more things in at a faster pace.[/p][p]What the main focus of Chapter 3 is will [b]definitely [/b]be up to what players think, so we're leaving that pretty open for now even if we have some long-term ideas.[/p][p]When exactly [b]Early Access [/b]ends and we release into 1.0 is still undecided - we shall see what the future holds.[/p][p][/p][p][i]But the updates will not stop.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Some items in Chapter 1 and 2 are pretty self-explanatory, or will be expanded upon as they get released in a specific update (Endless Mode for example) but we can briefly talk about some things:[/p][p][/p][p][b]Sector Modifiers[/b] is a system where we can add modifiers to whole missions depending on where they are in the galaxy regions, to make the world feel more alive and challenges more dynamic and interesting.[/p][p]This could be "Increased Legion Activity" where all enemy squads are Elite-class, "Ion Storm" where weather events are more common or Materia costs are increased, or something that causes stronger Artifacts to appear. Stuff like that.[/p][p]We've got some fun ideas for the Modifiers system when we implement it fully.[/p][p][/p][p]The [b]Scanner Revamp [/b]will happen as we aren't happy with how little functionality it offers at the moment. There's not a whole lot to do with it at the moment, and it's not as fun as being a Gunner. We have some ideas, like finding hidden caches of materials by scanning a vague anomaly somewhere on the map. Maybe spending time to scan/hack an enemy ship (with a mini-game) gives it one of several debuffs.[/p][p][/p][p]If you have any feedback on the roadmap itself or want something more minor to be listed, please let us know! (Chat with us in Discord pls). Again, our development plan can always change and your most popular requests may sneak themselves into chapters.[/p][p][/p][p]We sincerely hope you will support us through the launch, Early Access, and beyond![/p][p][b]Wishlist now and join us at launch on September 19th![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Over and out![/p][p]- The Keepsake Crew[/p]

notes.title: We're rebranding to Jump Space!
notes.notes: [p]TLDR: Our game name is now Jump Space, due to trademark complications.[/p][p]We also have over 1 million Steam Wishlists! Release date announcement is happening on August 20th, during the FGS Gamescom stream.[/p][p][/p][h3]Hello again, Jumpers![/h3][p]We hope you have enjoyed your summer~[/p][p][/p][p]Today we have very important things to talk about, so let's dive right in:[/p][p][/p][h3]🚨The game rebrands to [b]Jump Space🚨[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Long story short - Jump Space is the final name following trademark complications.[/p][p][/p][p]We think [b]Jump Space [/b]is super cool, after all, there is more to the game than just the [b]Ship[/b]![/p][p][/p][h3]Please help us spread the word so that everyone hears about the name change![/h3][p][/p][p]This also gives us a great excuse to show off the new [b]keyart [/b]we had planned for Early Access launch![/p][p][i]Pretty Michael Bay-esq, huh?[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/5adcd866e32ead62fe6b8c3388e53e6d010c989d.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]This name change will not impact[b] [/b]our release plans for Jump Space.[/h3][p][/p][h3]In fact, [i][b]Release Date Announcement[/b][/i] will drop during Gamescom later in August! ːsteamhappyː[/h3][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Now for MORE positive and INCREDIBLE news![/p][p][/p][h3]1 Million Wishlists.[/h3][p][/p][p]That's quite the number.[/p][p]One that most developers don't think is reachable before it's time to release.[/p][p][/p][p]"Happy to see that my repeated gnome disassembler sacrifices payed off. Thanks for your service, Nisse ❤️"[/p][p]- Rasmus, 3D Artist[/p][p][/p][p]The magic and excitement of having players so eager to play your game never goes away.[/p][p]Especially not for a passion project like Jump Space.[/p][p][/p][p]We managed to get enough traction to build a great team around the game, and we can only be extremely grateful for the opportunities we've been given.[/p][p][/p][p]This game is our very own baby, and seeing it reach these numbers is... Yeah, it's crazytown.[/p][p][/p][p]We've sure come a long way since the first 5 of us first moved into this space.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/0b29097f9236a1ab743ef30d24ae88a4c0d3044d.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Thank you.[/b][/h3][p](You will continue to hear this in every post for the next 6 months - Just get used to it.)[/p][p][/p][p]Now - we've seen the wishlist numbers climb through the years, so this didn't [i]fully[/i] come out of nowhere.[/p][p]We see what people want from the game, and we have really cool plans for what to add beyond Early Access launch.[/p][p][/p][p][i]If you stick around for this journey with us, you shan't be disappointed.[/i][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]In honor of this milestone, we wanted to share a few more images from the past.[/p][p]Can you believe Jump Space looked like this by the end of 2021?[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/6223639eb82de4ddb35c6de063b5da4a213c1795.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Asserting dominance over the power grid, barely any textures, ship cannons firing JPGs.[/i][/p][p]This is just how it goes![/p][p]You keep cooking and then you end up with how the game looks now ːsummercrab2023ː[/p][p][/p][p]We are in the final stretch before Jump Space Early Access now, y'all.[/p][p][i](Is the new name setting in yet?)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Gamescom can't come soon enough![/p][p][b][i]Danke und auf Wiedersehen.[/i][/b][/p][p][/p][h3]- The Keepsake Crew[/h3]

notes.title: Demo Retrospective + Addressing the Most Common Feedback!
notes.notes:
[h3]How's it going, Jumpers? [/h3][p]Don't forget to drink water.[/p][p][/p][p]By the time you read this [b]we will have closed the Demo, meaning it will no longer be playable.[/b][/p][p]We sincerely hope you've enjoyed this little taste of Jump Space over the last few weeks.[/p][p][/p][p]As we will get into below, there's a lot of improvements we will make between now and Early Access launch. We can deliver a much better experience, [i]and we don't want you to burn out on just a handful of missions[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][i]Absence makes the heart grow fonder, after all.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]So how did Next Fest go??[/b][/h3][h3][b]What funky little stats do we have from the Demo?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Check it out:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/267ea77b2a9185bdffea832417abd900c5d41031.png"][/img][/p][p]We are currently at over [b]950K wishlists [/b]which is a crazy number.[/p][p]Getting 1 million before launching is something we never considered remotely feasible - but here we are maybe going to see it happen.[/p][p]Landing at the [b]Top #3 Demo[/b] spot during Next Fest made us very, very happy.[/p][p]The hard work seems to have been worth it.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][u][b]Responding to the most common feedback points of the demo![/b][/u][/h2][p][/p][p]First and foremost - thank you for leaving all your feedback and suggestions in Discord, our form or on Steam. We've tried to read as much of it as possible, and we feel we have a great grasp of what you like and what should be improved ASAP to make the best experience possible.[/p][p]Shoutout to you who sent crash reports in Discord if you ran into a rare weird crash - hammering those out before launch is great, to ensure a smooth launch for 100% of players.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="2iXll2rDsuM;full"][/previewyoutube][p]We wanted to jump into addressing the most common feedback topics right away, cause we're serious about improving the game, y'all!
So Groove and Filip Coulianos from the team sat down and went through the [i]20-or-so[/i] most feedback-iest points and give answers to how we're fixing those things specifically.[/p][p][/p][p][b]If you don't feel like watching the video above, we'll lay out each topic and answer here:[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]1. Roguelite elements / "Why don't we keep the stuff we find into the next mission?"[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A: [/b]This is a big priority for us. Even though we will stick to our core of missions being Roguelite in design, we can certainly fix the frustration of not being rewarded for collecting things. Converting collected loot and unused items into Credits by mission end is the very least we can do, and that will be added to the main game.[/p][p][/p][p][i]Just for context of why we straight up don't let you keep things:[/i][/p][p]Keeping all gear between missions will have players quickly finding the best MK3 weapons and being permanently too powerful. That just makes every mission too easy and the challenge of the game falls apart.[/p][p]We have a design solution that we are confident will make both the Roguelite enjoyers and Roguelite dislikers happy. We can't talk about it yet, as we have to implement and test it first.[/p][p]It's okay for us to break the mold and try something in the middle-ground that makes the most sense for the game.[/p][p]But as mentioned, we think this design fix will be super good and also enhance this "Space Fantasy" we are striving for with the game.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]2. Aim-Assist is weird / Playing on controller has several issues, Keybinding etc.[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] First and foremost - sorry![/p][p]The controller experience has not been as prioritized as it should have been, but rest assured that all of these technical issues as well as keybinding struggles will be fixed.[/p][p]Players will undoubtedly run into more problems that we haven't thought about, but we will fix these on the fly going forward - because we do care![/p][p]And regarding the magnetic, super strong aim-assist: We will add a slider for this and just make it behave normally.[/p][p]Rest assured - we will fix ːsteamthumbsupː[/p][p][/p][h3][b]3. Solo Play is difficulty / BuddyBot is unhelpful and wastes ammo[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Absolutely true, we agree with this.[/p][p]For context: BuddyBot was a feature we had on our roadmap, but were not planning on implementing this early.[/p][p]During closed beta, [b]WAY[/b] more players than we expected wanted to play at least partially solo, so we had to - in a short amount of time - jam BuddyBot in to start testing solo play.[/p][p]He is a very new feature, so of course players have run into pain points.[/p][p]We are working on BuddyBot right now to make sure he doesn't shoot into asteroids or spend your hard-earned Materia in stupid ways. We just finished making him able to craft repair kits![/p][p]We will improve Buddy over time, with the goal of eventually having him be able to do every task that a normal player can.[/p][p]So as this happens, Solo play will get more stable and balanced, and we will of course look into any other difficulty scaling tweaks we need to make.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]4. Upping Player Limit to 6-8 Players[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] It's not the highest priority. What limits us most is game design, rather than anything technical.[/p][p]We've made everything with max 4 people in mind, so for larger crews we'd have to think about new, specific mission types that feel suitable, otherwise people will have nothing to do or things might get too easy - it's a fine line to walk.[/p][p]We want to make sure the game runs great, feels good, has all the features we want before we can start thinking about 5+ players.[/p][p]At some point in the future we will talk about it and see if the game can be adapted.[/p][p]We're also curious to see going forward if a larger part of the playerbase will request this, or if it's only a vocal minority that want 5+ players.[/p][p]We assume people majorly want max 4 players, but if we are wrong then we have to make sure we can start working on that sooner. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]5. Sliding while on-foot, more movement[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Yes, it's coming.[/p][p]Might not be in exactly at Early Access launch but very soon after.[/p][p]We wanna make it a BIG DEAL lol, and send it off with flying colors.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]6. Matchingmaking or Lobby Browser?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Lobby Browser is coming to Early Access.[/p][p]This was another thing was de-prioritized a little bit because testers actually didn't seem to mind, and lobbied up by inviting through Steam Friends.[/p][p]We will let you have a Public or Private lobby, where you can name it something funny and hope people join or specify what kind of players you want to play with (tryhards or casuals).[/p][p]We think this is a better allocation of our resources than doing an algorithm-matchmaking thingy.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]7. Endless Mode[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Short answer is Yes![/p][p]Maybe not included right at Early Access launch but coming soon after.[/p][p]There will be several ways of playing Endless (we're not confident enough to share all the details yet)[/p][p]Maybe Challenge Rating above 5? It just keeps going? Who knows...[/p][p]We haven't decided on whether we want a save feature in Endless, so you can leave and continue that run later. Or if we want it to be a non-stop gauntlet and you have to commit to several hours of HARDCORE in one sitting to beat the record.[/p][p]Maybe both?[/p][p][/p][h3][b]8. Smart-Pings?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] It's not on our immediate roadmap.[/p][p]There are other, easier aspects we can improve, like coloring pings to player colors to see who pinged what.[/p][p]Hopefully you can supplement all your communication needs with the text chat.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]9. 1st Person Pilot View / Free Look[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] That's been a requested feature for maybe a year now, and something we want as well.[/p][p]We're just about getting to it on the to-do list, so if it's not in for Early Access launch, it will come shortly after. We're very excited to have it, we want that IMMERSION, BABY.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]10. More for Pilots and Scanner users to do[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We absolutely recognize that since dodging things isn't super consistent, sometimes the pilot only points and shoots, and the Scanner is extremely basic right now.[/p][p]The Pilot dogfighting gameplay is quite a high priority. Allowing players to avoid and dodge things is something we're working on right now. A new engine component in Early Access will give the Pilot flares that you can drop, to counter homing missiles for example.[/p][p]A silent engine for more sneaking, engines that might have much more Boost - stuff like that is coming![/p][p][/p][p]The Scanner will receive other components in Early Access that will make it much more interesting. You can call in Supply Beacons every X amount of jumps from the Scanner. Another will be able to mark enemy ships which will increase damage dealt to them.[/p][p]The basic Scanner functionality in itself will receive a design rework at some point, to make it more immersive and interesting. Have more hidden things that forces you to use the Scanner and stuff like that.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]11. FPS Combat feels a little basic[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We have a lot of ideas floating around for adding further spice to this (grenades, turrets etc.)[/p][p]A common request has been a dedicated melee weapon, which we will add![/p][p]We have a wrench model that we're just about to put in, but we definitely want to make melee a more viable strategy and maybe even necessary for some enemy types.[/p][p]Another aspect of this is enemy variety.[/p][p]We have a few enemies right now that do more than just stand and shoot, but we want to explore and widen up the types of enemies you're facing and how they force you as players to play differently to overcome them.[/p][p]Internally, the team has always been like "We need something like the Left4Dead Witch, that'd be so coool!"[/p][p]So we might take some inspiration there, but cooler enemy variety is definitely coming as well.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]12. Official Flight Stick / HOTAS support[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Short answer is maybe![/p][p]We'll have to follow the statistics on this one.[/p][p]We've heard many, many requests for this, but in the grand scheme of things perhaps this is a vocal minority and we are better of prioritizing it further into the future (but hey if you're a HOTAS enjoyer reading this - we want it just as much as you do, we just gotta prioritize <3)[/p][p]At some point we will do it, unless modders add super good support for it before we can.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]13. Text Chat and Voice Chat[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We are working on text chat right now, because it's a must-have.[/p][p]With voice chat, we have our great Discord server and we'd like as many of you as possible to use that or other reliable way to have voice comms.[/p][p]So voice is not something for the immediate future. At some point later we'll probably add it, but for now it doesn't feel as critical as text chat.[/p][p]Maybe by then we have an idea for a cool proximity filter effect to add more immersion! ːsteamthumbsupː[/p][p][/p][h3][b]14. More Graphics Options[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b]  Absolutely![/p][p]This was just one of those things that didn't make it into the demo, but of course we want even potato PCs to run the game as well as possible.[/p][p]More options will come, whole bunch of boxes to uncheck and Gamma sliders, don't you worry.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]15. "Please add a Big Player Ship with Smaller Fighter Ships inside"[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We had something similar in the earliest prototype of the game![/p][p](Search "[b]HyperSpace : Pirates of Atira - Flying Hauler Drone" [/b]on YouTube to find it)[/p][p]That drone was kinda slow, so it was removed from the core design of Jump Ship, but the fantasy is still alive![/p][p]What we are looking into is maybe making a component that can spawn a remote-controlled device or tiny ship. So that you can act out that fantasy not just in a big ship with a cargo bay but in any ship.[/p][p]Much designing on that is still left to do but [b]TLDR; Before we are done with Jump Ship, we will add small fighter ships somehow.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]16. Power Grid layout resetting after every mission[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We have made that change now, so in Early Access the power grid will NOT keep resetting![/p][p]We will also add a Power Grid representation in the hangar itself a bit later, so that you can preview the layout and fix it before you even start a mission.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]17. "Let us enter the Ship while it's sitting in the Hangar!"[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We knooow! It's so tempting but we force you to jump to your doom just to get close to it![/p][p]Entering the ship in the hangar is [b][i]purely[/i][/b][i] [/i]a technical issue.[/p][p]For example, the host can cycle between ships in the hangar once you've unlocked more than 1 ship.[/p][p]If another player is already inside the ship while it's being swapped out, what happens then?[/p][p]Stuff like that. The ship is basically a level by itself.[/p][p]We want that fantasy as well, but it's a big technical thing to solve.[/p][p]We'll leave it for later in the future, since it's more of a "cool to have" and the game is great even without that feature.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]18. More opportunities to join missions / be able to rejoin immediately after a disconnect[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Trust us - forcing players to wait until the next jump in the mission happens for you to be able to join the session is [b]NOT [/b]a design choice - it's another technical limitation.[/p][p]The game is technically complicated, with our large map sizes and players being able to spread out kilometers apart. Syncing all that data to a new player that's just joining has proven to be a big challenge.[/p][p]Which is why currently it's way easier for us to only allow players to join when a jump happens, since then we only need to sync all player positions inside the ship and make sure all that is the same across all connections in the session.[/p][p]We can probably solve this piece-by-piece going forward.[/p][p]Meaning that later on we can allow players to join mid-bubble but only when all players are inside the ship and not in combat [i]for example. [/i]Later we can increase that "okay when X or Y isn't happening, then players can join regardless of where everyone else is on the map."[/p][p]Give us time to overcome the technical obstacles and we'll improve the mid-mission joining.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]19. Ship Shields are confusing and so are some components[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We've heard a lot about players not understanding how the Shield Generator or "Protected Power" mechanic works, and that's totally valid.[/p][p]We've reworked the ship shield system many times, and we're [b]STILL [/b]not happy with how it works right now. It will be reworked yet again between now and Early Access.[/p][p]Can't talk about it too much, but shields will be more of a Pilot responsibility and not just another flat, dull health bar.[/p][p]Many components that you haven't seen yet also lack clear descriptions, so that's something we will work on. Helpful tooltips for how everything works, which includes explaining protected power.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]20. Tutorial Improvements[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A: [/b]This goes hand-in-hand with the above topic of not explaining everything clearly.[/p][p]We sort of want players to figure some stuff out themselves outside of the prologue tutorial. For example, the prologue doesn't talk to you about the gunner seat, but eventually most players jump into it and figure out it's intended use.[/p][p]We also strongly keep in mind that most people probably don't want to sit in a 30-minute tutorial in a co-op game when their friends are waiting. So keeping the tutorial as brief as possible while explaining the critical, very core concepts is a fine line to walk.[/p][p]When it comes to the issue of players not feeling like they understand mechanics or systems, that's something we can solve with UI or UX improvements, better tooltips rather than making the tutorial needlessly THICK with explaining that you might not even remember.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]21. Iris and Buddy talk way too much[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]A: [/b]Believe us - they used to talk way more.[/p][p]I think we just default to a lot of voice lines to confirm that voice events trigger when they're supposed to, and then we just leave it like that lol.[/p][p]We can definitely look into that, maybe by adding a slider for Buddy and Iris, or by just cutting their chatter by half in general.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Phew![/p][p]I hope that's put your concerns to rest and gotten you [i]even more[/i] excited about the looming Early Access launch of Jump Ship.[/p][p][/p][h3]That's all for now![/h3][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for an announcement regarding launch date - it won't be long now![/p][p]After that we'll post a detailed Roadmap to let you know what features that will make it into the launch build of the game, and what will be added during "Year 1" and in what order.[/p][p][/p][p]Fly safe during summer, Jumpers.[/p][p][/p][p]- The Keepsake Crew[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/7b43c34d1c9a79ca0b8be7343ee7355c90b3ecc1.png"][/img][/p][p](INCREDIBLE fanart by @mattdezine from our Discord)[/p]

Happy Friday, Jumpers!

Today we have some real good stuff to announce.

notes.title: Enemy Ships in Jump Ship
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=tR9-1K7R9AA;full][/previewyoutube]
Greetings space lovers!
In Jump Ship, you'll face a diverse array of enemy ships designed to make every encounter as dynamic as possible. They come in different sizes, shapes and fire power. We're currently testing four main ship types, each with unique roles and challenges. Keep in mind that everything is a work in progress, so designs, names, and numbers might change as we refine the experience.

The current four types are:
[list]
[*] Cannon Fodder
[*] Fighters
[*] Gun Ships
[*] Corvette
[/list]

[b]Cannon Fodder[/b]
Cannon Fodder ships are small, fast, and agile. They don’t have much health or firepower, but their speed and movement make them tricky to target. They’re easy to kill when you land a hit.

[b]Fighters[/b]
Fighters are the most common ships you’ll encounter, and we currently have two variants:[b] light fighters[/b] and [b]heavy fighters[/b]. Light fighters are fast and armed with autocannons, while heavy fighters are bulkier and pack more firepower, making them tougher opponents.

[b]Gunships[/b]
Gunships offer the most variety in terms of abilities and challenges. We’re experimenting with several types, including [b]autocannon gunships, missile gunships, sniper gunships[/b], and two distinct [b]mine layers[/b].

[b]Missile gunships[/b] unleash a barrage of homing missiles, forcing you to dodge and lose them in the chaos. 

[b]Sniper gunships[/b], on the other hand, are long-range predators equipped with railguns. They stay at a distance, waiting for the perfect shot, then reposition after firing a devastating blast. They will try to escape if you get too close to them.

[b]Mine layers[/b] bring a different kind of danger. Some deploy explosive mines in the air, while others launch infiltrator missiles that attach to your ship’s hull and release enemy units onboard. If you don’t destroy the mines in time, you’ll have to deal with enemies wreaking havoc inside your ship.

We’re also testing a [b]support gunship[/b] that shields other enemy ships, making it a priority target when it appears.

[b]The Corvette[/b]
Corvettes are the largest enemy ships in the current roster. The broadside corvette we have now circles your ship, firing powerful missile salvos from its sides. These ships add another layer of strategy, as your crew can board them for an on-foot battle to take them down.

Oh btw, you can actually board most of the enemy ships mentioned above, and deal direct damage to them if you prefer :)

Have a nice weekend
xoxo

notes.title: Chaos in Space: Jump Ship Playtest Insights
notes.notes:
For those new to our community, Jump Ship is a co-op PvE where you are the crew of a space ship. We're thrilled to share some insights from our recent office playtest.

[h2]Recent playtest[/h2]
Last Friday, we had an office playtest for Jump Ship. Our goal was to evaluate the game's readability and how well it communicates information to new players. We want Jump Ship to be enjoyable and playable without any prior knowledge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/f632aa28f9e89e64b598f06a29fbcc26d784d539.png[/img]
[i]Big fans visiting the office[/i]

The playtest involved testing the the tutorial and one of the game's missions.

[h2]Key Insights[/h2]
Our playtest provided valuable feedback on readability for sure, and overall status:
[list]
[*] The game is incredibly fun! The players were laughing throughout the session :)
[*] The chaos level is currently too high, leading to some confusion.
[*] Some items and their uses weren't immediately clear to players.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958487/93669256de1ba570fe82b2547dc6964f0a5f2ff0.png[/img]

[h2]Our action plan[/h2]
Based on these findings, we're already working on:
[list]
[*] Refining the chaos: We want the game to be chaotic, but in the right way. Players should understand why events occur and how to take action. We're improving the HUD to highlight critical information and provide more context for items in hand or in use.
[*] Balancing intensity: We're reducing simultaneous chaotic events to prevent overwhelming players.
[*] Clearer item descriptions: We're rewriting descriptions to be more direct and informative.
[/list]

[h2]What's next?[/h2]
We're planning another playtest soon to evaluate these improvements. Our focus is on smoothing out the gameplay experience and making it easier for new players to jump in.

The feedback has been instrumental in shaping these priorities. We're committed to creating the best space crew experience possible and we're excited to invite more community testers eventually and hear what you think!

Do you already have ideas on how we can make the game more accessible to new players? Let us know :)

Thank you for your continued support and enthusiasm. Together, we're creating an amazing universe!

notes.title: May the fourth be with you!
notes.notes:
It's May the 4th, the international Star Wars day!

Jump Ship draws inspiration from many different sources, including Star Wars. When friends ask us what kind of co-op game we're building, we sometimes describe Jump Ship as the ultimate Chewbacca and Han Solo experience—the duo that somehow always makes it through tight situations. That's the feeling we want you to have when playing the game with your friends!

So, what have we been up to? We've been reworking parts of the ship combat, the combat station, and player ship damage. I know this probably doesn't make much sense for you right now, since you can't test the game, but we'd like to give you some behind the scenes regardless :) 

[b]Please note, recorded directly from dev's computer in a dev level. Nothing is final![/b]

[previewyoutube=hDyo3P6bqLk;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]General combat[/b]
[list]
[*]Depending on how close the crosshair is to the enemy ship's sweet spot (indicated by the small dot moving ahead of the ship) you can get critical, normal and glancing hits. They produced 3x, 1x, 0.5x damage respectively. Tracking enemy ships and consecutively doing critical hits kills much faster.
[*]Not all things has a sweet spot (stationary targets, and very large ships, in those cases all hits defaults to normal hits). We can set that up manually per ship/target.
[*]AI shields now regenerate after a given amount of time incentivising use of shield penetrating weapons, or boarding if you lack those types of weapons. We currently lack indications of this in the HUD. (As this is more of a feature to incentivise use of combat station or boarding regeneration doesn't happen when playing solo).
[*]AI Corvettes no longer shoot long range missiles when downed.
[*]AI Corvettes has a further orbit distance to ensure that players can't attack the corvette sitting still, they'd have to move towards it and chase it to take it down.
[*]For ship to ship combat we now have a damage counter that accumulates damage up to 2 seconds and then clears to better indicate the amount of damage dealt by your different weapons.
[/list]

[b]Pilot[/b]
[list]
[*]Auto aim crosshair no longer snaps to target. You will have to steer the playership crosshair to enemy ships to hitting them.
[/list]

[previewyoutube=1Rw9aNYHs9Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Combat station[/b]
[list]
[*]Combat station now supports up to two sockets with larger cannons or other components.
[*]We replaced the old autocannon with a railgun. A powerful insta-hit attack that penetrates enemies shields and damages the hull directly.
[*]We reintroduced a active ship shield that can be triggered from the combat station that keeps damage to 0 for a set amount of time.
[*]You can swap between items using numericals (1-3). You can install two railguns, or two shields if you'd like.
[*]Auto aim crosshair no longer snaps to target. You will have to properly aim crosshair to enemy ships to hitting them.
[*]When aiming using the railgun turret, the pilot will see a laser pointer indicating where you are aiming to help the pilot assist the combat station.
[/list]

[b]Player ship damage[/b]
[list]
[*]Instead of gradually damaging components and damage points we now trigger "events" (read internal explosions) at intervals where several things may break simultaneously.
[*]These events are somewhat concentrated around areas of the ship and will be more varied than before (some damage points where never picked etc.).
[*]Damage point types cycle, so getting same type of damage points breaking down over and over should be much less likely.
[/list]

notes.title: 100 000 x THANK YOU! And some frequently asked questions answered
notes.notes:
Hi friends!
I'm [url=https://twitter.com/Kappische]@kappische[/url], one of the devs here at Keepsake. I just wanted to write down some words to summarize our greatest regards to everyone who has wishlisted, provided feedback, and asked questions since launching the page last week.

We've received over 100,000 wishlists within the first week! That's an amazing start, so thank you very much! Our goal was to reach 100,000 wishlists when launching into Early Access. To achieve that within a week exceeded our expectations and dreams! We celebrated the reveal in the office and have been reading your comments, feedback, and questions. Thank you very much for this!

In future posts I'm hoping to go a bit more behind the scenes and treat this space as a dev log so you can tag along on the development of the game.

Below are some of the questions we've received, along with their answers:

[b]What can you do on the ship?[/b]
We're always thinking of and expanding on the various activities you can do on the ship. These include installing/uninstalling components, rerouting energy, disposing of items, using airlocks/eject tubes, make pizza, manning turrets, and more. I'm hoping to show you activities in a future video rather than just listing things here :)

[b]Can you play solo?[/b]
Yes, you can. The game scales depending on the number of players. However, playing co-op will provide the best experience since that's what we're tuning the game for.

[b]When will the game be released?[/b]
We haven't decided on a specific date yet. We'll provide more information later. Currently, we're targeting late 2024 for Early Access.

[b]Are there other types of enemies than robots?[/b]
The current on-foot enemy types you encounter are robots. They will appear in different configurations that we'll reveal more about in the future. Human adversaries are something we'd like to explore in the future, but it's out of scope for the Early Access launch since our team is quite small and we need to prioritize accordingly. 

[b]What will the game cost?[/b]
We haven't finalized the price yet, but it will be in the ballpark of other 4-player co-op games of similar scope. Final pricing details will be announced at a later date.

[b]How long will you be in Early Access?[/b]
Our intention is to use Early Access as a way to finalize the game together with the feedback from you all in the community. We will stay in Early Access until we are satisfied the game has the polish, features and content we feel it should have for a 1.0 release, but even after that our plan is to continue the development of the game with bugfixes and content.

[b]On what platforms will you release?[/b]
We've announced Steam (Windows) and Xbox releases so far. We'll consider other platforms in the future.

[b]Why no PvP?[/b]
We personally enjoy PvE games, and unfortunately, implementing PvP is a very costly endeavor that we're not prioritizing. The game isn't designed for PvP, and it would essentially require starting over and creating a new project to make PvP work properly.

Keep the questions and feedback coming!
Thank you!
/Daniel
